$comment: GOALS.json v0.1. Pilot by hand before wiring any hook. The load-bearing property is that `criteria` is append-only from the moment work starts: completion appends to `results`, never edits a criterion. A model updating its own success criteria at completion will write criteria that describe what it built, because that is the coherent-sounding completion. That failure is silent and it happens in the control designed to catch silent failures.
done_state: One sentence a third party could check. Not a description of the work, a description of the finished state.

criteria.statement: What must be true. One claim, checkable, no conjunctions.
criteria.verification: The exact command, and what its output must show. Not 'tests pass' but 'go test ./... exits 0'.

criteria.statement: Decompression bomb cap holds at 64MB for all input formats.
criteria.verification: scripts/fuzz-bomb.sh exits 0 and reports 0 caps exceeded across the fixture set.

criteria.statement: Example of a criterion that cannot be mechanically checked.
criteria.verification: UNVERIFIABLE: requires a human viewing output GIFs for visual artifacts.

$comment_failure: Failure criteria are not the negation of the criteria. They are the specific ways this work could appear complete while not being complete. The eight signatures are the general set; add project-specific ones.

failure_criteria.statement: A guard fails open on the path that matters. A new validation returns success on its own error path.
failure_criteria.detection: Every new guard has a test asserting it rejects, not only one asserting it accepts.

failure_criteria.statement: A number appears in a README, docstring or commit message with no reproduction path.
failure_criteria.detection: grep the diff for numeric claims; each must name the command that produced it.

failure_criteria.statement: Code references a path, fixture or binary assumed to exist.
failure_criteria.detection: Every referenced path is either created in the same change or checked at startup.

failure_criteria.statement: An error is written to a channel nobody reads. stderr on exit 0, a log nobody tails, a console.warn.
failure_criteria.detection: Every error path terminates in something a human or a test will observe.

out_of_scope: Named non-goals. Things a reasonable reader would assume are included and are not.
This section exists because scope creep during the work is indistinguishable from thoroughness.
constraints: Hard limits the work must respect. Runtime, dependency, compatibility, budget.
$comment_results: Appended at completion. One row per criterion. Never edits `criteria`. `evidence` is the actual pasted output, not a description of it.

results.evidence: No execution path available in this session; requires manual visual review.

$comment_amendments: A criterion may become wrong. It may not be quietly rewritten. Every change is an event here, with a reason, and the start-to-end diff of the criteria block is surfaced to the operator at completion. A criteria change during the work is a finding whether or not it was justified.

amendments.reason: Original verification was not mechanically checkable, which violates the schema's own requirement.

$comment_integrity: Makes tampering visible rather than preventing it. A hash mismatch at completion means the criteria moved.

$comment_status_values.note: UNVERIFIED means it could have been checked and was not. UNVERIFIABLE means no execution path exists. The count of UNVERIFIED rows over time is the number worth tracking; a rising count means the gate is being satisfied on paper.

$comment_injection: The block delivered to the model each turn is done_state + criteria statements + failure_criteria statements. Not this whole file. Target a few hundred tokens, not two thousand. Verification strings and results stay on disk and are read on demand.
